title: Handley Page Halifax DT696
memorial_type: Board / Plaque / Tablet: brass plaque on wooden backboard
memorial_details: A brass plaque on a wooden backboard hangs in St Helen's church, Stillingfleet. It was dedicated on 14 February 2008 and unveiled by H N Mottershead, President of the 158 Squadron Association. It gives Flood's rank as P/O, repeating a CWGC error. A second memorial stone placed near the crash site was mistakenly moved to a nearby farm, according to Yorkshire Aircraft.
inscription: DEDICATED TO THE CREW OF/ RAF HALIFAX DT696/ OF 158 SQUADRON/ WHO DIED NEAR STILLINGFLEET/ ON SUNDAY 14TH FEBRUARY 1943./ (Names...)/ THEIR NAMES LIVETH FOR EVERMORE.
narrative: Halifax DT696 of 158 Squadron took off from Rufforth at 18.16 on the evening of 14 February 1943, bound for Cologne. One port engine failed soon after take-off. The bombs were jettisoned near Appleton Roebuck, but the heavily loaded aircraft stalled and crashed at 18.30 just west of Stillingfleet. All seven crew were killed.
